column3: NASB puts “just as he had done … to Ai and its king” in parentheses; “utterly destroyed” renders the verb for devoting to destruction, and “within their land” renders “in their midst.”
“he feared” is singular for the Hebrew plural “they feared”; “mighty” renders “warriors.”
“abandon” renders “let your hands drop from”; “that live” renders “the inhabitants of.”
“by marching all night” renders “all the night he had gone up.”
“confounded” renders “routed”; “He slew them” renders “he struck them,” whose subject may be Israel.
NASB moves “at Gibeon” after “stand still”; “stand still” renders “be still.”
“stopped” renders “stood still”; “the sky” renders “the heavens,” and “go down” renders “go.”
“had fled and hidden” uses the pluperfect.
“do not stay there yourselves” renders “and you, do not stand”; “delivered” renders “given.”
“slaying them with a very great slaughter” renders “striking them a very great defeat.”
“No one uttered a word against” renders “No one sharpened his tongue against.”
“at sunset” renders “at the time of the going of the sun”; “to this very day” renders “until the substance of this day.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB reads “it” for the Hebrew “them.”
